name: Poor Law Unions 5 Apr 1891
description: The 160 Poor Law Unions of Ireland at the census of 5 Apr 1891, as Table VI of each 1891 county report lists them. The same unions stood from the dissolution of Gortin on 1 Apr 1889 until Glin was dissolved on 30 Sep 1891. Each union is drawn as the 1907-12 District Electoral Divisions (Phelim Birch's and Paddy Matthews's maps) that cover its 1891 divisions, matched by name from hand transcriptions of the printed tables (Mayo and Sligo from OCR, checked by hand). Each union carries its land area (land_acres: the map area less large lakes and tideway, which the census also leaves out), the sum of its printed county-part acreages (census_acres), the difference (pct_diff) and a confidence grade. All 160 unions can be checked: 156 agree within 1% (142 within 0.5%; median 0.08%); Belfast (+6.7%, reclaimed foreshore inside the later city wards), Wexford (+4.8%, reclaimed slobs), Donegal (-3.0%, Lough Eask counted by the census) and Glenties (+1.8%) are further out. The King's County and Queen's County divisions are from Table VI of their own 1891 reports. Carlow agrees exactly: its printed 1891 total of 185,155 acres matches the map; the 199,998 acres of 1911 include Cranemore and Clonegall, which joined the union between 1891 and 1901. The map is simplified for display by a coverage simplification of the division map, so neighbouring unions keep common edges (95% of divisions lie within 10 m of the full lines); the full-resolution file is among the downloads.
